transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place, but... I guess I'm here because, well, for the last couple of years I've just been feeling kind of low all the time? 

I mean, I try really hard not to let it show, and I'm still doing everything I'm supposed to. I go to work, and church, and I spend time with the people I care about... but even then, there's just this heavy, empty feeling that doesn't really lift. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds like I'm just complaining, but... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you can help with?
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that activities you once looked forward to now feel empty or unfulfilling?

Um, actually, I don't think so? I mean, I still really try to enjoy things. Like, when I'm hanging out with my friends or doing things with my church group, I still smile and have a good time. I definitely don't want to seem ungrateful for the good things in my life, you know? So I make sure to appreciate them. 

It's not really that the activities themselves feel unfulfilling... it's just more of that heavy background feeling I mentioned before. I still like my hobbies and everything. Is... is that okay? I hope I'm answering your question right, I just don't want to make it sound worse than it is.
Can you describe how your mood has been over the past few days or weeks? Does the low feeling come and go, or has it been pretty much constant during the time you’ve been feeling this way?

Well, um, it's pretty much been constant, I guess? Like I said, it's just this heavy background feeling that's always there, even when I'm smiling and doing okay. I try really hard not to let it get to me, though. 

As for how long... um, I guess it's been about two years and four months now? It started right around the time I had to stop taking my community college classes. The money just wasn't working out, and with my schedule as an inspector at the plant, it was just too much to juggle. I mean, I know a lot of people have to work and can't afford school, so I shouldn't really complain about it. I'm lucky to have a job at all, right? But... yeah, I think that's when this constant low feeling started. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired or that you have less energy than usual, even when you haven’t been doing anything particularly strenuous?

Um, yeah, I guess I have been pretty tired lately. I mean, I know working at the plant is tiring for everyone, so I try not to make a big deal out of it. But... it feels like even the small stuff just drains me? 

Like, just filling out the inspection logs at work, or driving to play basketball, or even just... washing my hair. It all feels like it takes more energy than I actually have. And even when I try to rest on my days off, I don't really feel... refilled, I guess? 

I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't be complaining when I'm just sitting around doing normal things. I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. Is it normal to feel that tired from just everyday stuff?
Have you found yourself feeling like you're not good enough, or that you're letting people down, even when there's no real reason for it?

Oh, um... no, I don't really think I feel that way? I mean, I try really hard to do a good job at the plant and be there for my friends, so I don't think I'm letting anyone down. I always make sure to pull my own weight. 

I know I'm not perfect or anything, but I don't really walk around feeling like I'm not good enough. I just try to do my best with what I have, you know? I hope it's okay that my answer is no for that one. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on, and I definitely don't want to complain about things that aren't actually happening. Is that helpful?
Have you had any periods, even brief ones, when your mood was not low at all—where you felt genuinely okay or even good—for a day or more?

Um, honestly, no. I don't think I've had any days where I felt totally fine, not for a long time. I mean, I have moments where I'm smiling or laughing with my friends when we play basketball, and I try to focus on those good parts. I really do try to be positive and not bring people down. 

But as far as having a whole day where that heavy background feeling is just... gone? No, I don't think so. It's always kind of sitting there underneath everything else. I hope that's an okay answer. I don't want to sound like I'm just being dramatic or not trying hard enough to be happy. Is it normal for it to just stay like that all the time?
Can you recall if your mood ever changes at all in response to positive events, like seeing friends or being praised at work, even a little bit, or does it just stay the same most of the time?

Um, I'm not really sure? I mean... I definitely smile and I always say thank you when my supervisor says I did a good job on the inspection lines, or when I'm hanging out with my friends. I really try to show that I appreciate it, because I don't want them to think I'm ungrateful or anything. 

But... inside, I don't think the actual feeling really shifts. It just kind of stays the same most of the time, even when I know I should be feeling happy about something good happening. 

I'm sorry, I know I should be reacting better to the positive stuff in my life. I really do try to focus on it. I just... I hope I'm explaining that right, and I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for. Does that make sense?

Can you think of a time in the past few months when something really good happened—like a celebration or a nice surprise—where you felt a clear, strong sense of joy or excitement, even for a little while?

Um, a really good thing... well, my friend had a birthday party a couple of weeks ago, and it was really nice. I helped her set up and everything, and everyone was having a really good time. I made sure to be involved and celebrate with her, because she's a great friend and I wanted it to be special for her. 

But as far as feeling a strong sense of joy or excitement... um, I don't think I really felt that way, even though I knew it was a happy occasion. I just kind of felt the same as I always do, just going through the motions, I guess. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds terrible, like I'm a bad friend or something. I really did want to be happy for her, and I hope I didn't ruin the mood or anything. I just... I don't think I can really feel those strong happy feelings right now. Is it okay that I answered that way? I just want to be honest with you.
Can you tell me if you've noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, even things you used to really like, like your hobbies or spending time with friends?

Um... I mean, I still go to everything. I still play basketball with my friends, and I still try to keep up with all my hobbies, because I don't want to be the person who just drops out of everyone's life, you know? I want to be a good friend and keep trying. 

But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, it doesn't really feel the same as it used to. It's like I'm doing the things I know I'm supposed to enjoy, but the actual enjoyment part is just... missing? Like I'm just going through the steps. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or like I'm not appreciating my friends. I swear I'm still trying my best to be present and have fun. I just... it's just harder to feel it lately. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering these questions right.
Can you confirm that, over the past two years, your mood has been consistently low without any extended periods—like several weeks or more—where you felt noticeably better or back to your usual self?

Um, yes, I think that's right. I mean, I really try not to let it show, and I hope I haven't been bringing anyone down, but... yeah, it's been consistently like this for a while now. 

I guess it's been about two years and four months? It started right around the time I had to stop taking my classes at the community college. I just couldn't make the money work with my schedule at the inspection lines, and I had to drop out. I've tried really hard to just keep my head down and work hard since then, but... I haven't really had any breaks where I felt like my old self again, even for a few weeks. 

I'm sorry, I know I should be handling things better, and I really am trying to push through it. I hope it's okay that it's been going on for that long without me fixing it. Is that the kind of timeline you were asking about?
Can you tell me if you've noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, even things you used to really like, like your hobbies or spending time with friends?

Um... oh, I think we might have just talked about this a little bit? I'm so sorry, I hope I didn't answer it wrong the first time. 

Like I was saying before with the basketball and everything... I really do still try to show up and do all my hobbies, because I don't want to let anybody down or be a burden. It's just that the actual fun part of it feels like it's gone right now. 

Did... did you need me to explain it differently, or did you mean something else? I'm really sorry if I didn't give you enough detail before. I can try to think of a better way to describe it if that's what you need? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you tell me if there are any activities or hobbies that you used to really enjoy but don't enjoy as much anymore?

Um... I feel like I'm repeating myself, and I'm really sorry if I'm not giving you the answers you're looking for. I really want to be helpful. 

I don't think there's anything specific that I've stopped enjoying completely, or like... a specific hobby that stands out. It's more just that general feeling I was trying to describe before, where everything just feels a little flat, even though I'm still trying my hardest to do them all. 

I still go to basketball, I still try to read, I still hang out with my friends... I really haven't dropped anything, I promise. I don't want to be the kind of person who just gives up on things. Is that okay? Should I try to think of something specific? I really don't want to mess up this evaluation.

Can you recall if your mood ever lifts, even just a little, during particularly happy moments—like when you're laughing with friends or receiving praise—or does it tend to stay at the same low level no matter what’s happening around you?

Um, well... I mean, I really try to let myself feel happy when good things happen. Like, if I'm with my friends and they're joking around, I definitely laugh and try to be part of it. I don't want to bring the mood down or make them feel like I'm not appreciating them. 

But... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope this doesn't sound ungrateful, it kind of feels like I'm just going through the motions? Like, I smile and I laugh, but inside, that heavy, flat feeling doesn't really go away. It just sort of stays there underneath everything. 

I'm sorry, I know I should be able to just enjoy the good moments like a normal person. Am I explaining that right? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I really do try to be positive.
Can you think of a time when you used to really look forward to something—like a hobby, event, or time with friends—and now it just doesn’t feel the same or doesn’t bring you the same satisfaction?

Oh... gosh, I am so, so sorry. I feel like I'm really frustrating you because I know you've kind of asked me about this a few times now, and I must be doing a really bad job of explaining myself. I'm really trying, I promise. 

Um... to answer your question, I honestly can't think of a specific time or a certain event that I used to look forward to and now don't. I just don't really have a specific example like that to give you. It feels like I've just been pushing through and doing my best to show up for things for so long that I don't really remember a clear 'before' and 'after', if that makes sense? 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a specific memory to point to. I can keep trying to think of one if you really need it for your notes? I just don't want to make something up and give you the wrong information. Am I... am I answering these okay? I really don't want to be making your job harder.

inference_history.note: The patient reports a persistent low mood over several years with preserved functioning, suggesting consideration of persistent depressive disorder (F34.1) or recurrent major depressive disorder (F33.9). Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.22) and major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified (F32.9) are also possible given the nonspecific onset and duration.

The persistent and constant low mood over several years, along with increased fatigue and lack of energy, makes chronic depressive disorders (F33.9, F34.1) more likely. Major depressive disorder (F32.9) is less likely given the absence of clear episodes or more severe symptoms, and adjustment disorder (F43.22) is less likely due to the duration and consistency of symptoms beyond a typical stressor response.

The patient reports persistent low mood, anhedonia (diminished enjoyment in activities), and fatigue, with symptoms lasting over two years. This rules out F33.9 (Major Depressive Disorder, single episode, unspecified) due to the chronic nature of symptoms favoring F33.1 (Dysthymia) or F34.1 (Persistent Depressive Disorder).
